A positivity conjecture of Prellberg and Stanton

Thomas Prellberg Address: School of Mathematical Sciences, Queen Mary University of London, London E1 4NS, United Kingdom Email address: t.prellberg@qmul.ac.uk
Date: October 8, 2026
Abstract.

We prove the conjecture of Prellberg and Stanton (2003) that 1−q(qn,q)m​[nm]q\frac{1-q}{(q^{n};q)_{m}}\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{n}{m}_{q} has nonnegative power-series coefficients for 0<m<n0<m<n, except when nn is even and m∈{2,n−2}m\in\{2,n-2\}. We obtain a polynomial version by bounding a Möbius correction by first differences of Gaussian coefficients. The proof uses partitions and quadratic and cubic semi-invariants of binary forms. An extension of this bound proves the Reiner–Stanton–White conjecture on positivity of orbit polynomials for flags of subspaces.

Key words and phrases: 
Gaussian polynomial, integer partition, semi-invariant, Singer cycle
2020 Mathematics Subject Classification
Primary 05A17; Secondary 05A30, 13A50

1. Introduction

The purpose of this paper is to prove a conjecture of Prellberg and Stanton [20, Conjecture 1] on the monotonicity of partition counts. The same method proves the conjecture of Reiner, Stanton and White [21, Conjecture 10.3] on orbit polynomials for flags of subspaces.

We use the notation [r]q=(1−qr)/(1−q)[r]_{q}=(1-q^{r})/(1-q), (x,q)r=∏j=0r−1(1−x​qj)(x;q)_{r}=\prod_{j=0}^{r-1}(1-xq^{j}), and [nr]q=(q,q)n/((q,q)r​(q,q)n−r)\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{n}{r}_{q}=(q;q)_{n}/((q;q)_{r}(q;q)_{n-r}). Throughout, ℕ={0,1,2,…}\mathbb{N}=\{0,1,2,\ldots\} and P≥qQP\mathrel{\geq_{q}}Q means that P−QP-Q has nonnegative coefficients.

Prellberg and Stanton [20] proved that, for odd n≥3n\geq 3, the number of partitions of NN with parts in {n,n+1,…,2​n−1}\{n,n+1,\ldots,2n-1\} is nondecreasing for N≥1N\geq 1. This continued the study of partition monotonicity in Friedman, Joichi and Stanton [9]. Prellberg and Stanton also conjectured that

Fn,m​(q)=1−q(qn,q)m​[nm]qF_{n,m}(q)=\frac{1-q}{(q^{n};q)_{m}}\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{n}{m}_{q}

has nonnegative coefficients for 0<m<n0<m<n, except when nn is even and m∈{2,n−2}m\in\{2,n-2\}.

Here is the partition interpretation. Let an,m​(N)a_{n,m}(N) count partitions of NN with parts in {1,…,n−m}∪{n,…,n+m−1}\{1,\ldots,n-m\}\cup\{n,\ldots,n+m-1\}, using at most mm parts from the first interval. The small parts fit in an m×(n−m)m\times(n-m) rectangle; the large parts have unrestricted multiplicities. Thus

∑N≥0an,m​(N)​qN=[nm]q(qn,q)m,[qN]​Fn,m=an,m​(N)−an,m​(N−1),\sum_{N\geq 0}a_{n,m}(N)q^{N}=\frac{\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{n}{m}_{q}}{(q^{n};q)_{m}},\qquad[q^{N}]F_{n,m}=a_{n,m}(N)-a_{n,m}(N-1),

where an,m​(−1)=0a_{n,m}(-1)=0. The conjecture says that these partition counts are nondecreasing. We prove the following polynomial version.

Theorem 1.

For 0<m<n0<m<n, except when nn is even and m∈{2,n−2}m\in\{2,n-2\}, the polynomial

has nonnegative integer coefficients. Consequently Fn,m∈ℕ⁡[[q]]F_{n,m}\in\mathbb{N}[[q]] for all these pairs.

For m=1m=1, we have Fn,1=1F_{n,1}=1. For m≥2m\geq 2, the consequence follows from

(1) Fn,m=Rn,m(1−qm⁡(n+1))​(qn+2,q)m−2(m≥2).F_{n,m}=\frac{R_{n,m}}{(1-q^{m(n+1)})(q^{n+2};q)_{m-2}}\qquad(m\geq 2).

At q=1q=1,

Rn,m​(1)=mn​(nm)=(n−1m−1),R_{n,m}(1)=\frac{m}{n}\binom{n}{m}=\binom{n-1}{m-1},

the number of compositions of nn into mm positive parts. We do not yet have a natural statistic on these compositions, or a direct partition model, whose generating function is Rn,mR_{n,m} in general. Section 5 gives a Dyck-path construction in the coprime case and asks for a construction in the remaining cases. Such a model, together with (1), would also count the first differences of an,m​(N)a_{n,m}(N) directly.

The coprime case of Theorem 1 follows from the positivity of [nm]q/[n]q\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{n}{m}_{q}/[n]_{q}, the rational qq-Catalan polynomial associated with the coprime pair (m,n−m)(m,n-m); see Haiman [14, Propositions 2.5.3 and 2.5.4] and Andrews [1]. More generally, if g=gcd⁡(n,m)g=\gcd(n,m), then [g]q​[nm]q/[n]q∈ℕ⁡[q][g]_{q}\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{n}{m}_{q}/[n]_{q}\in\mathbb{N}[q] by Brunetti and Del Lungo [4]; see also Chen and Hou [5, Theorem 8] and Guo and Krattenthaler [13, Lemma 5.2]. To obtain Rn,mR_{n,m} from this quotient, one multiplies by [m]qn+1/[g]q[m]_{q^{n+1}}/[g]_{q}. For g>1g>1 this is a polynomial with coefficient −1-1 at qq, so the known positivity does not suffice.

We will subtract a Möbius correction from a Gaussian polynomial and bound that correction by the Gaussian first differences. Sylvester’s theorem identifies these differences with dimensions of spaces of semi-invariants. We use quadratic and cubic semi-invariants with the bidegrees of the independent family constructed by Jafari and Najafi Amin [15]. For related comparisons of Gaussian polynomials, see Chen and Jia [6, 7]; strict unimodality and quantitative lower bounds were studied by Pak and Panova [18, 19].

Section 2 bounds AA by first differences of GG. Section 3 uses this bound to prove Theorem 2. Corollary 1 gives the subspace case of the orbit-polynomial conjecture, and Section 4 proves the result for flags. Armstrong [2, Section 11.2] discusses the subspace case and proposes a further coefficientwise monotonicity conjecture.

3. Positivity of the corrected quotient

The following division lemma turns symmetric unimodality into positivity of a quotient.

Lemma 3.

Let r,τr,\tau be positive integers and let P∈ℕ⁡[q]P\in\mathbb{N}[q] be symmetric and unimodal. If P/[r]qτP/[r]_{q^{\tau}} is a polynomial, it belongs to ℕ⁡[q]\mathbb{N}[q].

Proof.

This is [13, Lemma 5.1], with exponents τ\tau and r​τr\tau. We include the short argument. Write P=∑j=0Dpj​qjP=\sum_{j=0}^{D}p_{j}q^{j} with pj=pD−jp_{j}=p_{D-j}, allowing zero coefficients at both ends, and set pj=0p_{j}=0 outside [0,D][0,D]. Below the midpoint of the quotient its coefficient at kk is

∑t≥0(pk−t​r​τ−pk−τ−t​r​τ)≥0.\sum_{t\geq 0}(p_{k-tr\tau}-p_{k-\tau-tr\tau})\geq 0.

All indices lie at or below (D−(r−1)​τ)/2≤D/2(D-(r-1)\tau)/2\leq D/2, where the coefficients of PP are nondecreasing. Symmetry gives nonnegativity for the remaining coefficients. Division by the monic polynomial [r]qτ[r]_{q^{\tau}} gives integrality. This also covers a specified centre with zero coefficients at both ends, and the case P=0P=0. ∎

Proof of Theorem 2.

Lemma 2 gives A∈ℕ⁡[q]A\in\mathbb{N}[q] for all n>mn>m. For HH, we first prove polynomiality and remove the small widths. We then write HH as a sum of two nonnegative polynomials.

1. Polynomiality. Let ζ\zeta have order e|me\mid m, with e>1e>1. For d|gd\mid g, the order of ζd\zeta^{d} is e′=e/gcd⁡(e,d)e^{\prime}=e/\gcd(e,d), and e′|m/de^{\prime}\mid m/d. The qq-Lucas evaluation [22, Theorem 2.2, pp. 131–132] (see also the earlier proofs [17, 8]) therefore gives Qd​(ζ)=0Q_{d}(\zeta)=0, including G⁡(ζ)=0G(\zeta)=0 when d=1d=1. If e|ne\mid n, the same evaluation gives

G⁡(ζ)=f⁡(e),Qd​(ζ)=f⁡(lcm⁡(d,e)),f⁡(t)=(n/t−1m/t−1).G(\zeta)=f(e),\qquad Q_{d}(\zeta)=f(\lcm(d,e)),\qquad f(t)=\binom{n/t-1}{m/t-1}.

5. Remarks and questions

Theorem 1 leaves several combinatorial questions. We first compare its product formula with other positivity results. Gatzweiler and Krattenthaler [11] study quotients of Gaussian polynomials with a common top argument (Conjecture 1), and products ∏i(1−qr+i)ai/(1−qi)ai\prod_{i}(1-q^{r+i})^{a_{i}}/(1-q^{i})^{a_{i}} with a symmetric exponent sequence (Conjecture 3). The latter extend Stanton’s fake Gaussian sequences [23]. In Rn,mR_{n,m} the factor [m]qn+1[m]_{q^{n+1}} dilates the exponents of [m]q[m]_{q}; in those products a common shift translates the degrees. We do not identify Rn,mR_{n,m} as a specialization of either family. For cyclotomic generating functions more generally, see Billey and Swanson [3] and Gatzweiler, Levicán-Santibáñez and Yoshida [12].

There is a simple obstruction to applying the regular-sequence criterion of [12, Proposition 3.3] to the product

Rn,m=(1−qm​C)​∏j=n−m+1n−1(1−qj)(1−qC)​∏j=2m(1−qj),C=n+1R_{n,m}=\frac{(1-q^{mC})\prod_{j=n-m+1}^{n-1}(1-q^{j})}{(1-q^{C})\prod_{j=2}^{m}(1-q^{j})},\qquad C=n+1

for m≥2m\geq 2. The criterion requires every selection of denominator degrees to generate an additive monoid containing at least as many numerator degrees, counted with multiplicity. Suppose g=gcd⁡(n,m)>1g=\gcd(n,m)>1. Select the m/g+1m/g+1 denominator degrees C,g,2​g,…,mC,g,2g,\ldots,m. They generate ⟨g,C⟩\langle g,C\rangle. Below CC, this monoid contains only multiples of gg, so it contains exactly m/g−1m/g-1 degrees from the numerator interval and also the degree m​CmC. There are only m/gm/g such numerator degrees. Thus the criterion fails whenever g>1g>1, even in positive cases such as (n,m)=(6,3)(n,m)=(6,3). This concerns the displayed product; another Hilbert-series realization may still be possible.

At q=1q=1 there is an elementary necklace interpretation. Let 𝒩n,mprim\mathcal{N}_{n,m}^{\rm prim} be the binary necklaces of length nn with mm ones and least period nn. Möbius inversion on repetitions, followed by division by the orbit size nn, gives

#​𝒩n,mprim=1n​∑d|gμ⁡(d)​(n/dm/d),G⁡(1)−A⁡(1)=m​#​𝒩n,mprim.\#\mathcal{N}_{n,m}^{\rm prim}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{d\mid g}\mu(d)\binom{n/d}{m/d},\qquad G(1)-A(1)=m\,\#\mathcal{N}_{n,m}^{\rm prim}.

The second equality uses (n/d−1m/d−1)=(m/n)​(n/dm/d)\binom{n/d-1}{m/d-1}=(m/n)\binom{n/d}{m/d}. Lemma 2 interprets G−AG-A at general qq as the weight enumerator of subsets outside ⋃p|gXp\bigcup_{p\mid g}X_{p}. It would be interesting to find a cyclic action and a compatible statistic giving a cyclic-sieving interpretation of these polynomials.

A direct proof of the original conjecture would give an injection between successive partition sets. Let 𝒫n,m​(N)\mathcal{P}_{n,m}(N) be the set counted by an,m​(N)a_{n,m}(N).

Problem 1.

For each nonexceptional pair 0<m<n0<m<n, give a uniform combinatorial rule for an injection from 𝒫n,m​(N)\mathcal{P}_{n,m}(N) into 𝒫n,m​(N+1)\mathcal{P}_{n,m}(N+1) for every N≥0N\geq 0.

The polynomial version suggests a second question.

Problem 2.

Find a natural nonnegative integer statistic on compositions of nn into mm positive parts such that, for every nonexceptional pair 0<m<n0<m<n,

Rn,m​(q)=∑a1+⋯+am=na1,…,am≥1qstat⁡(a1,…,am).R_{n,m}(q)=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}a_{1}+\cdots+a_{m}=n\\ a_{1},\ldots,a_{m}\geq 1\end{subarray}}q^{\operatorname{stat}(a_{1},\ldots,a_{m})}.

Since Rn,m​(1)=(n−1m−1)R_{n,m}(1)=\binom{n-1}{m-1}, Theorem 1 permits an arbitrary assignment of exponents to compositions. We ask for a direct combinatorial rule. When m≥2m\geq 2, one could then use (1) to count an,m​(N)−an,m​(N−1)a_{n,m}(N)-a_{n,m}(N-1) by adjoining a partition with parts in {m⁡(n+1)}∪{n+2,…,n+m−1}\{m(n+1)\}\cup\{n+2,\ldots,n+m-1\}, the latter set being empty for m=2m=2.

There is such a statistic when n,mn,m are coprime. The rational shuffle theorem [16] and the specialization in Garsia–Leven–Wallach–Xin [10, identity (I.1)] give

1[m]q​[n−1m−1]q=∑D∈𝒟m,n−mqcoarea⁡(D)+dinv⁡(D).\frac{1}{[m]_{q}}\genfrac{[}{]}{0.0pt}{}{n-1}{m-1}_{q}=\sum_{D\in\mathcal{D}_{m,n-m}}q^{\operatorname{coarea}(D)+\operatorname{dinv}(D)}.

Here 𝒟m,n−m\mathcal{D}_{m,n-m} consists of Dyck paths above the diagonal in the m×(n−m)m\times(n-m) rectangle, with the statistics of [10]. Given a composition (a1,…,am)(a_{1},\ldots,a_{m}), the cycle lemma gives a unique cyclic rotation of (a1−1,…,am−1)(a_{1}-1,\ldots,a_{m}-1) encoding the numbers of north steps before successive east steps of a path DD. Let j∈{0,…,m−1}j\in\{0,\ldots,m-1\} count the left cyclic rotations taking this encoding back to the original tuple. Then

stat⁡(a1,…,am)=(n+1)​j+coarea⁡(D)+dinv⁡(D)\operatorname{stat}(a_{1},\ldots,a_{m})=(n+1)j+\operatorname{coarea}(D)+\operatorname{dinv}(D)

has generating polynomial Rn,mR_{n,m}. The remaining question is to find a rule for the noncoprime pairs.
